slides.title: Got an offer on your Laval home? Read this.
slides.sub: From Saint-François to Sainte-Dorothée, here's how a promise to purchase works.

photo.credit: Église Saint-François-de-Sales, Saint-François · Photo: Jeangagnon, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.title: You have three ways to answer
slides.body: Not happy with the price or dates? A **counter-proposal** lets you reply with your own terms.

slides.title: Watch the acceptance deadline

banner.text: A date and time set in the offer

slides.body: Miss it and the promise is **cancelled**. Once you have it, the buyer can't withdraw it before then.

slides.title: Conditions protect the buyer
slides.body: Each condition has its own deadline. Until they're met or waived, the sale isn't final.

slides.title: Laval buyers have more to compare

photo.credit: Église Sainte-Dorothée · Photo: ndoduc, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: Active single-family listings in Laval are up **17%** year over year. Homes sold in **36 days** on average.

slides.title: The notary date is in the offer

photo.credit: Garden in Duvernay, Laval · Photo: Richard Mc Neil, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

slides.body: The promise sets the deed signing, occupancy date and adjustments. The buyer pays the notary and **welcome tax**.

slides.title: Got an offer? Let's read it together.
slides.tagline: I'll give it to you straight, no arrogance, no fluff.
